To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) perceiving a task-oriented goal structure in middle schools was associated with higher academic self-efficacious beliefs and lower academic self-consciousness; (b) these relations were mediated by personal task and relative ability goals; (c) perceiving positive teacher-students relationships was associated with more positive school-related affect; (d) these relations were partially mediated by school belonging; and (e) school belonging and academic efficacy were positively associated with school grades, and these relations were mediated in part by

(1) perceptions of the middle school psychological environment were related to adolescents' achievement goals, school belonging, and school-related affect, and that (2) adolescents' achievement goals and feelings school belonging in turn related to academic self- efficacy, academic self-consciousness, and academic grades.

(a) perceptions of the school learning environment were associated with adolescents' achievement goals and sense of belonging in school, and these variables were associated with school-related attitudes and achievement, and (b) the associations between perceptions of the learning environment and school-related attitudes and behavior were partially mediated through the achievement goals and sense or belonging that adolescents experienced in school.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the school learning environment affects students' psychological and behavioral functioning.
understanding the ways in which adolescents' perceptions of their school environment are related to their school-related beliefs and affect and their achievement outcomes.
the role of personal goals and feelings of belonging in mediating relations between perceptions of the middle-school psychological environment and school achievement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a task goal structure, positive teacher-student interactions, and a focus on mastery rather than relative ability goals in the middle school environment facilitate adolescents' academic self-efficacies and feelings of school-related belonging, which in turn promote positive school-related affect, and that these factors, in turn, are associated with academic achievement.
the school psychological environment is related to students' academic and social functioning through students' personal achievement goals and their sense of belonging in school.
the findings of this study support the idea that the school psychological environment is related to adolescents' school functioning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the school psychological environment, as it is perceived by students, is an important determinant of adolescents' psychological and behavioral functioning in school.

we have shown that students' perceptions of the psychological environment are related to their achievement goals, which in turn are related to their beliefs about their ability, their feelings about school, and their achievement.

the school psychological environment is important for the development of students' school-related beliefs, feelings, and behaviors, but the effects of the school psychological context are mediated by the goals that students set for themselves and the sense of belonging they feel in school.
The main takeaway from our work is that
schools can make a difference for students.
the middle school is an important context for adolescents' development.
schools should be places where students can feel a sense of belonging.
